title: Rome
completionText: You have survived Rome. The roads north beckon—Florence, Venice, and beyond await.

cards.dialogue: "The carriage rattles through the Porta del Popolo. Rome sprawls before you—ancient, eternal, and indifferent to your ambitions."
cards.leftText: You find rooms near the Piazza di Spagna. Economical, if somewhat damp.
cards.rightText: The Locanda dell'Orso welcomes you. Your fellow guests include a Prussian count.

cards.dialogue: "I can arrange a private viewing of the Belvedere Apollo—but His Holiness expects a donation to the restoration of San Giovanni in Laterano."
cards.leftText: The Cardinal's smile does not reach his eyes. Certain doors may now remain closed.
cards.rightText: The Apollo is more beautiful than any engraving suggested. You stand transfixed for an hour.

cards.dialogue: "Lord Pemberton's party invites you to dine. They speak loudly of home and seem uninterested in Rome itself—but their connections are formidable."
cards.leftText: You spend the evening at a trattoria, conversing with a Florentine antiquarian. More edifying, if less advantageous.
cards.rightText: The roast beef is overcooked and the conversation duller still—but you secure letters of introduction to Venice.

cards.dialogue: "These etchings capture Rome as she truly is—magnificent in decay. I offer you the complete Vedute at a price reflecting our mutual appreciation of the sublime."
cards.leftText: Piranesi shrugs. "The English buy them faster than I can print them."
cards.rightText: The portfolio is heavy but magnificent. You will study these for years.

cards.dialogue: "I know every stone of the Forum, signore. For a modest fee, I shall reveal secrets no guidebook contains. Though some prefer to wander alone..."
cards.leftText: You scramble over ruins until dusk, twisting an ankle on a fallen capital. The solitude was worth it.
cards.rightText: Giovanni's knowledge is encyclopaedic. He shows you inscriptions invisible to casual visitors.

cards.dialogue: "His Holiness Clement XIII grants audiences on Thursdays. A presentation could be arranged—though the appropriate... acknowledgments... would be expected."
cards.leftText: You watch others ascend the Scala Regia. Perhaps another Pope, another journey.
cards.rightText: You kiss the Fisherman's Ring. Clement speaks briefly of antiquities. The moment is transcendent.

cards.dialogue: "The mal'aria rises from the marshes in summer. You wake sweating, your head pounding. The English doctor recommends bleeding; the Italian suggests rest and broth."
cards.leftText: The bleeding weakens you further. Recovery takes three weeks.
cards.rightText: The broth is restorative. Within days you feel yourself again, wiser about Roman summers.

cards.dialogue: "In the Villa Doria Pamphilj gardens, you discover a sarcophagus bearing the inscription: ET IN ARCADIA EGO. A fellow visitor asks: 'What do you suppose it means?'"
cards.leftText: "Precisely," she says. "Even in Arcadia, I exist. A sobering thought." She introduces herself as Lady Mary.
cards.rightText: "A gentler reading," she smiles. "I prefer yours, though scholars disagree." A friendship begins.

cards.dialogue: "The most fashionable portrait painter in Rome offers to paint your likeness. The English queue for months. His fees reflect his reputation."
cards.leftText: You spend the scudi on books instead. Your appearance will fade; learning endures.
cards.rightText: Batoni positions you before a classical column, your hand resting on an antique bust. The image will outlast you.

cards.dialogue: "The catacombs beneath San Sebastiano hold the bones of martyrs and mysteries older than Rome herself. I can guide you—but the passages are narrow and the air unwholesome."
cards.leftText: You remain in the sunlight, conversing with pilgrims. Safer, if less remarkable.
cards.rightText: The skulls watch as you pass. You emerge shaken but enlightened about early Christianity.

cards.dialogue: "The gaming rooms are where fortunes change hands and reputations are made or destroyed. A Venetian merchant proposes a friendly wager at faro."
cards.leftText: You watch others win and lose. The merchant loses heavily; you are grateful for your caution.
cards.rightText: Cards fall and rise. By dawn the table has decided your fortune—for good or ill.

cards.dialogue: "I have acquired—through channels I cannot disclose—a manuscript claimed to be Cicero's own hand. Almost certainly genuine. The price reflects its rarity."
cards.leftText: The bookseller shrugs. "The English are less discerning." You wonder if you were too cautious.
cards.rightText: You sit with the manuscript by candlelight. Whether Cicero's hand or a forger's, it has changed you.

cards.dialogue: "Hadrian's Villa at Tivoli is essential—but the journey requires a full day and the roads harbour bandits. Will you join our party for safety, or venture alone at dawn?"
cards.leftText: The company is agreeable but slow. You see the villa through others' eyes as much as your own.
cards.rightText: The solitude is magnificent. You have Hadrian's dreams to yourself until noon.

cards.dialogue: "Michelangelo's ceiling overwhelms. A young artist beside you sketches furiously. 'Will you tell the guards?' he whispers. 'Copying is forbidden.'"
cards.leftText: You shield him from view. He shares his sketches later—and insights into Michelangelo's technique.
cards.rightText: You move away. The guards notice nothing. Prudence sometimes tastes like cowardice.

cards.dialogue: "The Colosseum by moonlight is Rome's most romantic experience. But the ruins harbour unsavoury characters after dark. A guide offers torchlit passage for a fee."
cards.leftText: You see the Colosseum as thousands have. Adequate, if unexceptional.
cards.rightText: The silver light transforms the arena into something sacred. You understand why poets weep here.

cards.dialogue: "Your time in Rome draws to a close. The roads to Florence beckon—but a collector offers to purchase your entire cabinet for a handsome sum. Will you travel lighter?"
cards.leftText: You depart Rome laden with memories and objects. The weight feels meaningful.
cards.rightText: Your purse is fat, your bags light. You wonder if you sold too cheaply.
